title: Ontario Revives Regional Immigration Pathway for Sudbury, Thunder Bay, Nipissing and Kenora
excerpt: The relaunched REDI initiative reserves Ontario nomination spaces for workers in six northern and rural communities until December 31, 2027. Quotas are not yet published, and the Workforce Priority Stream is currently the only active OINP route.
body:
• Ontario relaunched its Regional Economic Development through Immigration (REDI) initiative on October 16, reserving nomination spaces for workers in six communities: Greater Sudbury, Kenora, Nipissing, Rainy River, Renfrew County and Thunder Bay.
  • The initiative runs until December 31, 2027; the OINP has not yet published each community's quota.
  • Workers must qualify under an Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program stream — currently the Ontario Workforce Priority Stream is the only active pathway.
  • If you are an Indian worker or graduate in Canada open to the north: nearly 1,000 workers have been nominated through REDI to date, mainly in health care and the skilled trades.

Ontario will again steer provincial immigration nominations toward its northern and rural communities. The province announced on October 16 that it is relaunching the Regional Economic Development through Immigration (REDI) initiative, with dedicated nomination spaces reserved for workers in six communities who qualify under an Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program (OINP) stream, according to CIC News.

The six communities

The partner communities for the new round are Greater Sudbury, Kenora District, Nipissing District, Rainy River District, Renfrew County and Thunder Bay, with boundaries based on Statistics Canada census divisions. The province's REDI page says the initiative allocates spaces to communities that demonstrate a critical need for newcomer talent, and gives employers dedicated OINP support, including information sessions on using the programme to fill local labour needs. The OINP posted the new partner communities to its REDI page on October 14, ahead of the formal announcement, and confirmed the relaunch through its programme updates page.

https://x.com/canadavisa_com/status/2111167160714416298

How it works now

REDI operates as a quota of nomination spaces per community, running until December 31, 2027; the quotas themselves have not been published. The practical constraint is the state of the OINP after its 2026 overhaul: the Ontario Workforce Priority Stream, launched in June 2026 as the first stage of a two-phase restructuring, is currently the only active pathway through which foreign nationals can qualify. The earlier REDI round ran through the Employer Job Offer streams, which Ontario closed in May 2026, and the last REDI draw, on April 8, 2026, issued 32 invitations to candidates with a valid study or work permit and a job offer in Lanark or Leeds and Grenville.

The track record

REDI began as a pilot in 2020 with three communities, expanded in 2025, and has supported the nomination of nearly 1,000 workers to date, concentrated in health care and the skilled trades. Thunder Bay is the only community carried over from the previous round, which also included Lanark, Leeds and Grenville and Sarnia-Lambton.

Do not confuse it with the federal pilots

Three REDI regions overlap with federal programmes that are separate from the OINP and run on their own criteria: the Rural Community Immigration Pilot (Sudbury, North Bay area and Thunder Bay), the Francophone Community Immigration Pilot (Sudbury; French at NCLC 5 or higher), and the Francophone Minority Communities Student Pilot, whose participating institutions include Université Laurentienne and Collège Boréal in the Sudbury and Nipissing regions. For an Indian nurse, tradesperson or graduate already working in northern Ontario, the next step is to confirm the job sits inside a REDI census division and that the profile qualifies under the Workforce Priority Stream before the first draws are announced.
